svg.title: State — one conversation key: the LiveGeneration lifecycle plus the archive flag

g.text: State — one conversation key: the LiveGeneration lifecycle plus the archive flag
Guards are the real conditions in the code, not idealised ones
— every transition inside this region is reachable
correct but compares the single local identity to itself, because
nothing prevents a send on an archived conversation
token frame is retained for the generation's whole life so a
late attach can replay it. Nothing evicts it.
main.py:157: the answer is lost from history.
On the client, `attachStream`'s "already streaming" guard is
checked BEFORE the `await` at streams.ts:364, so the 8 s poll
can double-register and open two readers on one generation.
The old task is cancelled but
so its `finally` — including `db.add_message` — can run after the
new generation already replaced the registry entry.
awaiting the server call and never inspects `{stopped}`
(streams.ts:82-92); the promise is `.catch(() => undefined)`, so a
stop that silently fails leaves the GPU generating with no signal.
lock (compaction.py:258-260) while a detached background fold for
the previous turn may already be inside `_lock_for()` about to
`save_summary` — the measurement can be stale. The module
docstring's "they cannot double-fold or race each other"
(compaction.py:19-20) is true only of the fold itself.
`str(exc)` is sent to the browser verbatim — no sanitisation, no
several of them: the `NOT_FOUND_MODEL` regex ends in a bare
"report not found" (main.py:269) both render as *"The selected
model is not available on this machine right now."*
The Sidebar's Archived disclosure only renders when
`?archived=true`) can only fire from inside that section. A
conversation archived on another device is therefore invisible
until some other path caches it.
`lifespan` has no shutdown branch (main.py:27-38), so SIGTERM
kills in-flight generations without a terminal frame.
The client's own state machine is coarser —
no entry in `_live_generations` for this conv_key
engines.agent selected by the dispatch chain
SYNTHESIZE streams the merged answer as
browser tab closed / reloaded / navigated away.
The HTTP request ends; the task deliberately does NOT
whole buffer from index 0, then streams live
so it is waiting in history after reload (main.py:148-168)
Closing the SSE stream alone no longer stops the model
a NEW send on the same conv_key —
same two guards — cancel targets the task,
No `done` and no `error` frame; the client silently
re-measured, then sent to the model (compaction.py:149-167)
popover; `compact(force=True)` folds everything but the most
`db.save_summary()` upsert; the notice is parked in
model is `extra="forbid"` → 422 on an unknown key
frontend / edge — the client mirror of these states
orchestrator / app logic — live generation states
inference / GPU — a state entered by a model call
storage / data — a state that is a persisted row flag
Guards in [brackets] are the literal conditions in the source.
Bold text on a transition is the HTTP trigger.
Red notes = data loss, unbounded resource or security posture.
Amber notes = silent degradation, dead config or stale read.
